findings.finding: The platform documents programmable browser sessions, model selection, live views and high-level Stagehand automation primitives; the application builder is responsible for the agent's policy.
Browserbase presents sessions as isolated runtime units with project/session limits; documentation here does not establish that all external actions can be reversed after submission.
Browserbase documents per-session live view, logs, screenshots and replays to inspect agent behavior and debug failures.
A first-party Stagehand template uses an askHuman tool to pause the browser agent for user input and then resume; this is a template capability, not a mandatory platform-wide gate.
Browserbase documents browser, search and fetch infrastructure for agents handling workflows not exposed via conventional APIs, but does not quantify benefits for every deployment.
The Privacy Policy says browser data is not used to train generative AI models without affirmative consent; separately, customer-facing session recordings remain available for up to 30 days.
The August 2026 Trust Center notice adds ClickHouse for CDP log processing from September 14, except customers using BYOS for CDP logs; applicable customer configurations require clarification.
The platform documents a model gateway for multiple providers and an open-source Stagehand SDK, while execution remains dependent on Browserbase-hosted browser infrastructure unless replaced.
Published plans include free, $20 developer, $99 startup, and custom enterprise tiers with distinct usage meters and overage prices; actual invoices vary by use.
Enterprise documentation lists team SSO/SAML and live session inspection; the source does not measure collaboration or decision quality.

Browserbase explicitly promotes agents completing workflows humans formerly perform, including job applications and HR portal tasks; direction/magnitude of human impact cannot be inferred from marketing.
A free plan and open-source Stagehand SDK lower experimentation barriers, though free-plan browser time and concurrent capacity are limited.

limitations: The cited public company pages have been reviewed as text, not independently archived or cryptographically snapshotted.
Claims about features and policies do not establish performance in practice, actual individual harm or benefit, or legal compliance.
Impact/confidence codes were not assigned and no Humanity Score was computed or claimed.
Published legal/pricing policies may change and require confirmation at any commercial engagement.
correction_policy: Accept evidenced corrections and rerun the methodology; commercial payment does not buy any score change, favorable rating, or conclusion.
